prompt: Two collinear forces of magnitude 18 N and 28 N act on an object in opposite directions along the same straight line. State the magnitude and direction of the resultant force.

answer.text: 10 N in the direction of the 28 N force.

response_structure.guidance: State the numerical magnitude with unit and the direction relative to the forces.

mark_scheme: 1 mark: 10 N in the direction of the 28 N force (or opposite to the 18 N force).
hints: For opposing collinear vectors, subtract the smaller magnitude from the larger magnitude.
solution: Resultant = 28 N - 18 N = 10 N, directed in the direction of the larger (28 N) force.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 3: State direction: in the direction of the 28 N force. Award 1 mark.
lesson_anchors: Collinear vectors: addition along one line

abstract_patterns: resolving vectors into perpendicular components and vector addition/subtraction
provenance.independence_statement: Authored independently based on standard Cambridge AS Physics syllabus methods for vector resolution and addition.
